The State of Utah and the U.S. Forest Service are teaming up to provide $18 million to support Beaver County’s recovery.

RT by @RepMaloyUtah: On Pioneer Day, I had the opportunity to tour Beaver and see firsthand the devastating impact of both wildfire and flooding. Standing in those burned and flooded landscapes, talking with the Forest Service personnel, local leaders, and the people of Beaver one thing was crystal clear: forest management works. The difference between treated and untreated forest was visible. Areas that had been thinned or otherwise managed gave firefighters a chance. They slowed the fire, reduced its intensity, helped crews establish containment lines, and in some cases, stopped the fire altogether. In the overgrown, untreated areas, the fire burned hotter, moved faster, and left behind far greater destruction, burning an unprecedented 70,000 acres in two days. It's frustrating that while the United States is the world's largest importer of lumber and paper products, millions of acres of our own forests sit overcrowded and vulnerable to catastrophic wildfire. The boots-on-the-ground Forest Service personnel managing these forests know what needs to be done and want to actively manage these lands, but too often commonsense projects are delayed or stopped by endless litigation and opposition by environmentalists and bureaucrats in Washington D.C. That's why the Fix Our Forests Act deserves to move forward. The legislation passed the House with strong bipartisan support, but has been stalled in the Senate for 18 months. It needs to move forward. I'm grateful to Congresswoman Celeste Maloy for bringing us together to see this firsthand, and to the Trump Administration officials who came to Utah to witness these conditions on the ground. With the U.S. Forest Service headquarters coming to Utah, we have a tremendous opportunity to ensure the people making decisions about our forests are closer to the landscapes and communities they serve. Thank you to USDA's Michael Boren, Sam Crofts from the Bureau of Land Management, and Chairman Bruce Westerman of the House Natural Resources Committee for taking the time to be there and hear directly from those who have been impacted by this catastrophe. On Pioneer Day weekend, that lesson feels especially meaningful. The pioneers who settled this state understood that stewardship requires hard work, planning, and taking responsibility for the land we call home. We honor their legacy not by leaving our forests untouched until they burn and cause catastrophic damage, but by actively caring for them so they remain healthy for generations to come. The Beaver community continues to show incredible resilience. I was reminded why I'm so proud to be a Utahn. We face challenges head-on, we help our neighbors, and we don't shy away from doing the difficult work that's necessary to protect our communities and our public lands. @realDonaldTrump @RepMaloyUtah @RepWesterman @SenJohnCurtis @RepBurgessOwens @RepMikeKennedy @USDA @forestservice @Interior @BLMNational @NatResources @JStuartAdams @cralbrecht52 @BeaverCountyUT

RT by @RepMaloyUtah: Congresswoman Celeste Maloy toured the Cottonwood Fire burn scar in Beaver County today, telling KUTV's Samantha Hoffman the damage is extensive and warning that burn scar flooding remains a major concern for nearby communities. Maloy explained what comes next as local leaders work to assess the damage and begin the process of applying for FEMA grants to help with recovery. She was joined by Sen. John Curtis, House Natural Resources Committee Chairman Bruce Westerman, U.S. Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz and Interior Department Senior Adviser Sam Crofts, who discussed Utah's 2026 wildfire season, forest management and efforts to reduce the risk of future catastrophic fires. 🎥 Watch @KUTV2News @samhoffmannews #Utah #BeaverCounty #CottonwoodFire #Wildfire #CelesteMaloy #JohnCurtis #FEMA #FixOurForests

B001324.text: Is #TBT still cool? Throwing it back to my days as St. Louis County Prosecutor. No matter the role, I have always and will always fight for St. Louis. Lifting up our community is the most important thing to me.
A vaccine the size of a soda bottle?!  Once again, Trump proves he knows nothing about health care.  People should consult their doctors about proper vaccine protocol– NOT Donald Trump.

Generations of women fought to ensure they had the right to vote.  And now, Trump’s SAVE America Act threatens to block millions of women from voting.  I’m doing everything I can to stop it from passing and protect the freedom of every eligible voter.

The recent reports regarding our sailors and the living conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln are abhorrent and unacceptable. Trump's unauthorized war is endangering our brave servicemembers. This administration must ensure their well-being and safety. As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I am leading the fight to get answers and protect our troops.

My office fought hard to get a constituent with a high-risk pregnancy released from ICE custody, but this isn’t the end. It’s critical we ensure the safety of those in custody. I won’t stop fighting until the oversight work is done and the immigration process is fair and humane for everyone.

H001102.text: Over the course of this Congress, Democrats have had opportunity after opportunity to join us on popular, commonsense bills like the Stop Insider Trading Act. Yet time and again, they’ve proven they would rather put politics ahead of the American people.

President Trump and his administration are working day in and day out to reverse the damage of President Biden’s open-border policies. But tragedies like this are a stark reminder that Americans are still living with the consequences of an administration that allowed violent illegal aliens into our country who had no intention of pursuing the American dream or assimilating into our great country. It is imperative that we continue the work of deporting these dangerous individuals.

Our national debt just surpassed $40 trillion. That should be a wake-up call for everyone in Washington, Republican or Democrat. This did not happen overnight. For decades, Washington has spent beyond its means and passed the bill on to the next generation. We cannot continue down that path and expect America to remain the strongest nation in the world. Getting our fiscal house back in order means Congress has to get serious about reining in reckless spending and being responsible with the hard-earned money of the American people. I have consistently voted against unnecessary federal spending, and I will continue fighting to ensure we leave our children and grandchildren a stronger country, not a mountain of debt.

Under the Biden Admin, getting an abortion became as easy as walking to your mailbox. That’s why I introduced the Teleabortion Prevention Act to crack down on abortion by mail and require in-person care before abortion pills are provided. We must protect women and the unborn.

This is Deborah Murphy. She was a loving and vibrant grandmother and member of her community. While walking through a crosswalk at her local Publix, she was run over and killed by an illegal alien. Deborah is why I support ICE.
